land.text: Gujarat, Kathiawar and southern Rajasthan: the 43 growth of the Western Satraps is 1,330 of 1,331 cells cut from the Indo-Scythian shape

predecessors.note: Infobox predecessors: Indo-Scythians, Malavas and the Satavahana dynasty. Abhiraka (c. 35) is the earliest attested Kshaharata ruler.

land.text: Malwa, Gujarat and Saurashtra: Chandragupta II 'conquered Malwa after defeating the Western Kshatrapas' and likely reached 'the Arabian Sea coast in present-day Gujarat'

successors.note: Chandragupta II page: the victory 'can be tentatively dated to sometime between 397 and 409'.

land.text: the Kingdom of Valabhi of the infobox's successor list

successors.note: Infobox successors: Gupta Empire, Vakataka dynasty, Kalachuris of Mahishmati, Traikutaka dynasty, Kingdom of Valabhi. Cliopatria's Maitraka row starts in 476, 67 years after the last Satrap shape; the Vakataka page says Chandragupta II, with Vakataka support, 'annexed Gujarat from the Saka Satraps'.

capitals.name: Bharuch (Barygaza)
capitals.note: The infobox lists Ujjain, Bharuch and Minnagara without years. The Nahapana page has the Periplus call Minnagara the 'metropolis' of Nambanus's country around Barygaza but does not place it; Bharuch is used here for the Kshaharata period as a placeholder (confidence low). Reviewer (sa-02-c): extended to 126 because Ujjain lies outside Cliopatria's 43-126 shapes (it is in the 127 shape and in Cliopatria's Satavahana shape before); the Western Satraps page lists 'Ujjain Bharuch Minnagara' without dates.

capitals.name: Ujjain
capitals.note: Ptolemy places Chashtana's territory from Patalene to Ujjain ('Ozene, capital of king Chashtana'). The Rudradaman page says most scholars place his capital at Ujjain but there is no evidence for it. Reviewer (sa-02-c): the dot starts at 127, the first shape that contains Ujjain (75.79 E, 23.19 N); the page-based seat of Chastana (78-130, Ptolemy: 'Ozene, capital of king Chashtana') is earlier, but the drawn shapes of 43-126 do not reach it.

correction.text: the 43 shape unchanged, held from c. 35: Gujarat, Kathiawar and southern Rajasthan under Abhiraka and Bhumaka

keyframe_review.note: The infobox gives 'Established / disestablished: 35 / 415 CE' and lists Abhiraka (c. 35) as the earliest ruler; Cliopatria's first shape begins in 43. The 43 shape is held back eight years. The page gives no area for the state, so only the place is checked. Reviewer (sa-02-c): indo-scythians (sa-02-b) loses the same land to the Satraps only in 43 (its /ledger/13 and keyframe 43), so 35-42 is drawn in both dossiers; the page supports 35 ('Established: 35', 'c. 35: Abhiraka'), so indo-scythians should move its loss and the end of its keyframe 20 to 35 (reported to the orchestrator).

0.33 M km2: Gujarat, Saurashtra, Kutch, Rajasthan (41% of the shape) and western Malwa. The page puts Nahapana's land in Malwa, southern Gujarat, northern Konkan and the Nasik and Poona districts, from Bharuch to Sopara, and names neither Rajasthan nor Sindh for him; the shape holds none of Konkan, Nasik or Pune. Because the page dates Nahapana 24-70, 66-71 or 119-124, the shape cannot be tested against it; left as drawn.
Identical to 43 within 110 km2.
Identical to 43.

Identical to 43. The Nahapana page puts his coins' restriking by Gautamiputra (Jogalthambi hoard, Nashik district) and his fall at c. 124 (Dhavalikar), after 71 (Fynes) or in 78 (Bhandare); Cliopatria's Satavahana shapes -27 to 126 (890,000 km2) hold 1,200 of the 1,203 cells that the Satraps' shape gains in 127 (Konkan, Vidarbha, Malwa), and none of them is Satrap before 127. The reviewer (sa-02-c) asked for an adjust of the pre-124 keyframes plus a 124 loss here; not done because the Satavahana keyframes 106 and 110 (106-126) already hold these cells, so adding them here would draw Nahapana's lands twice in 106-123 unless satavahana-dynasty first subtracts them; the pair of dossiers must be settled together (see notes).

correction.text: the 127 shape without the Nasik and Pune districts: Rudradaman regained the former Nahapana territories except Poona and Nasik

keyframe_review.note: 0.62 M km2 (the page gives no area). The jump (+1,203 cells in Malwa, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Konkan, 1,201 of them) is the land Cliopatria's Satavahana shapes hold from -27 to 126. The Rudradaman page (r. 130-150) says he regained the former Nahapana territories except Poona and Nasik, yet the shape contains Nasik (85 of the 220 cells of a 100 km circle round Nasik plus an 80 km circle round Pune); the page's reign starts three years after Cliopatria's 127. Reviewer (sa-02-c): the ledger gain is now dated 127 too (Rudradaman's 130 in its note), matching this keyframe and satavahana-dynasty /ledger/5. The Junagadh list (150) also names Sindhu-Sauvira, Maru and Kukura, which Cliopatria draws as Kushan until 270 (see notes).

0.61 M km2: 45 cells (26 of them in Konkan) leave the shape, matching the Rudradaman page's marriage alliance in which he gave Aparanta (northern Konkan) to Vashishtiputra Satakarni as dowry (undated). Nasik is outside the shape from here to 223.
Identical to 154 within 1 cell.

0.47 M km2: 561 cells (eastern Madhya Pradesh, Malwa, Maharashtra) leave the shape, all of them into Cliopatria's Satavahana shape of 184. The page puts it in the late 2nd century Yajna Sri Satakarni (170-199 CE) defeated the Western Satraps and reconquered their southern regions (Western Satraps page); the Satavahana page says he 'recovered much of the territory lost' and that the Abhiras took the north around Nashik in the last years of his reign. 184 is in his reign.
Identical to 184 within 15 cells.

0.62 M km2: +616 cells, the lands lost in 184 and Nasik. The Satavahana page ends the main line at c. 224 (infobox 217-224) and splits it into five kingdoms, the western one around Nashik being the Abhira dynasty, so Nasik should not be Satrap; the Western Satraps page says Sanchi-Vidisha was re-established only under Rudrasena II (255-278), 30 years after this shape takes it. Left as drawn; the page does not date the Satraps' recovery. Reviewer (sa-02-c): the Nasik cells (43 of the 616) are now attributed to abhira-dynasty in the ledger; the Abhira dynasty page (read 2026-10-19) has the Abhiras ruling Nasik from 203 'with the help and consent of the Western Satraps', not under them.

0.51 M km2: 453 cells of the 224 shape go to Cliopatria's Vakataka shape. The Vakataka page puts Vindhyashakti at 250-270 and Pravarasena I (270-330) at the Narmada and Bundelkhand; it does not mention Sanchi or Vidisha. The shape still holds Vidisha and Sanchi, consistent with the Western Satraps page's rule there re-established under Rudrasena II (255-278).

0.84 M km2 (the largest): Sindh, southern Punjab and western Rajasthan (1,339 cells), all of them the Eastern Kushans' in 260. The Rudradaman page lists Sindhu-Sauvira (Sindh and Multan), Maru (Marwar) and Kukura (eastern Rajputana) among Rudradaman's lands in 150, so the shape's acquisition in 270 is 120 years after the page's date; see notes. No page dates 270.
0.78 M km2: 230 cells of Rajasthan go to Cliopatria's Yaudheya shape. The Rudradaman page says he subdued the Yaudheyas in present-day Haryana and that they later regained independence; undated.

0.50 M km2: 1,109 cells (Rajasthan, half of Sindh, southern Punjab) go to Cliopatria's Gupta shape of 347. Samudragupta's page (c. 335-375) has direct control from the Ravi east to the Brahmaputra, with a southwest line from Karnal to Bhilsa, Eran included (Majumdar's view); the shape keeps Eran and Vidisha, which the page suggests Samudragupta took from Sridharavarman (339-368). Left as drawn.
Differs from 347 by 38 cells (498,139 to 505,159 km2) at the edges; no page dates a change in 353.

0.51 M km2, identical to 353 within 4 cells. The Chandragupta II page puts the Gupta victory between 397 and 409 and dates Rudrasimha III's last coin to Shaka year 310 or 319 (388 or 397), consistent with the shape holding to 409.
The last shape, 407-409, identical to 383. The infobox gives 415 for the end; the Chandragupta II page tentatively 397-409 with coins of 409 carrying the Garuda; the dossier ends in 409.

correction.text: no Satrap territory exists after 409: this 55 km2 patch is to be dropped, not drawn; Saurashtra after 409 is Gupta and then Maitraka land

keyframe_review.note: A 55 km2 patch on the Kathiawar coast (71.29 E, 20.83 N) in 476-479. The page ends the state in 415 (infobox) and the Chandragupta II page says his campaigns 'brought an end to nearly four centuries of Saka rule'. The only Cliopatria neighbour is the Maitraka Dynasty (476-489); this is a stub, not a Satrap territory.

correction.text: no Satrap territory exists after 409: this 55 km2 patch is to be dropped, not drawn

keyframe_review.note: The same 55 km2 stub for 480-489; same reason.

ledger.note: c. 35: Abhiraka, the first known Kshaharata ruler, begins the Western Satraps in Gujarat and Kathiawar. The infobox gives established 35 and disestablished 415 CE and lists Abhiraka as ruler c. 35. Cliopatria's first shape is 43; the page gives no territory for Abhiraka, so the land is Cliopatria's.

c. 78: Chashtana founds the Kardamaka dynasty at Ujjain and the Saka era begins. Modern scholars widely equate the beginning of the Saka era with his ascension (possibly to Mahakshatrapa) in 78 CE; the Kshaharata line (Bhumaka, Nahapana) was the other major Saka Satrap line. The Kshaharata-to-Kardamaka succession is the Western Satraps page's own account; its dates for Nahapana (24-70, 66-71 or 119-124) do not fit a succession in 78.

region.text: Malwa, central Madhya Pradesh, northern Maharashtra and northern Konkan: Rudradaman's regained Nahapana lands without Poona and Nasik

ledger.note: c. 130, drawn from 127: Rudradaman I (r. 130-150) wins back the lands Gautamiputra Satakarni took from Nahapana. The Rudradaman page: he regained the former Nahapana territories except Poona and Nasik, repaired the Sudarshana lake and defeated Satakarni twice; the Junagadh inscription of 150 names Akaravanti (Malwa), Anupa, Anarta, Surashtra, Svabhra, Kachchha, Aparanta and Nishada. The Western Satraps page also says 'around 130 CE' he took the title Mahakshatrapa. Cliopatria's shape grows in 127 and satavahana-dynasty /ledger/5 records its loss in 127 (Higham: Gautamiputra 103-127), so the event is dated 127 to agree with the keyframe and the Satavahana loss; the page's year is three years later (confidence lowered from 2 to 1 for the year). Reviewer (sa-02-c).

region.text: the whole Satrap realm (Ujjain, Malwa, Gujarat, Saurashtra) held by Chastana's line

ledger.note: 127: the Satraps are drawn as vassals of the Kushans, the 'early period' of the Western Satraps page (re-read 2026-10-19): 'the position taken by modern scholarship is that the Western Satraps were vassals of the Kushans, at least in the early period until Rudradaman I conquered the Yaudheyas, who are usually thought to be Kushan vassals. The question is not considered perfectly settled'; the lead says it is 'still unclear whether the Western Satraps were independent rulers or vassals of the Kushan Empire'. The Rabatak inscription 'claims Kushan dominion over Western Satrap territory' under Kanishka (c. 127-150) and the Chastana statue found at Mathura 'suggests Castana may have been a feudatory of the Kushans' (undated; the Chastana page gives no date for any relation). 127 is Kanishka's year 1, the first Kushan claim to Ujjain; the page gives no start. Mirrored by kushan-empire /ledger (vassal_start 127, counterpart western-satraps). Added by the reviewer's finding (sa-02-c).

150: the Kushan suzerainty over the Satraps ends. The Western Satraps page ties the end of the 'early period' to Rudradaman I's conquest of the Yaudheyas, which it does not date; Rudradaman reigned 130-150 (Rudradaman page) and took the title Mahakshatrapa 'around 130 CE' (Western Satraps page), and his Junagadh inscription, which records the conquests, is dated 150. 150 is the last year of the reign and a bridging choice; a c. 130 end (the reviewer's suggestion) would leave three years of vassalage (127-129) and is not taken, because the page ties the end to the conquest, not to the title. Mirrored by kushan-empire /ledger (vassal_end 150).

c. 154: Aparanta, northern Konkan, passes to Vashishtiputra Satakarni. The Rudradaman page says his daughter married Vashishtiputra Satakarni and he gave Aparanta to Satakarni as dowry (Kanheri inscription); the page gives no year, and 154 is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the southern regions: eastern Madhya Pradesh, Malwa and Maharashtra

ledger.note: c. 184: Yajna Sri Satakarni reconquers the southern Satrap lands. In the late 2nd century Yajna Sri Satakarni (170-199 CE) defeated the Western Satraps and reconquered their southern regions (Western Satraps page); the Satavahana page says he 'recovered much of the territory lost' to the Satraps and that the Abhiras took the north around Nashik late in his reign. The page gives a reign, not a year; 184 is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Nasik: the 43 cells of the 224 growth within 150 km of Nasik

ledger.note: c. 224: Nasik enters the Satrap shape in the year Cliopatria's Satavahana row ends. The Satavahana page has the Abhiras take the north around Nashik (satavahana-dynasty /ledger/8 loses Nasik 150 km to abhira-dynasty in 203, and /ledger/9 hands the Satavahana shape to abhira-dynasty in 224); the Abhira dynasty page (read 2026-10-19) has them rule Nasik from 203 'with the help and consent of the Western Satraps (Sakas)' and says nothing of the Satraps taking it. The cells are Cliopatria's; the counterpart is the Abhiras, not the Satavahanas (reviewer, sa-02-c). The Abhira dynasty needs a dossier.

region.text: eastern Madhya Pradesh, Malwa and Maharashtra, the lands lost in 184 (573 cells, 557 of them in Cliopatria's Satavahana shape of 215)

ledger.note: c. 224: the Satraps take back the southern lands lost in 184 as Cliopatria's Satavahana row ends. The Satavahana page gives the end as c. 224 (infobox 217-224) and splits the empire into five kingdoms; nothing on it says the Satraps took any of it, and the Abhira dynasty page says the Abhiras 'gradually seized' Malwa 'from the Kshatrapas' (undated). Cliopatria shows the gain in 224. satavahana-dynasty has no matching loss to western-satraps (its /ledger/9 dissolve hands the 215 shape to abhira-dynasty); the pair needs either a Satavahana loss to the Satraps in 224 or a successor entry (reported). Confidence 1.

region.text: the 453 cells given to the Vakataka shape

ledger.note: c. 260: the Vakatakas take the eastern Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha border lands. Vakataka page: Vindhyashakti (r. 250-270) founded the family and Pravarasena I (270-330) 'carried his arms to the Narmada in the north'; the page does not say whom they displaced and does not mention the Satraps in the 3rd century. 260 is Cliopatria's year.

region.text: Sindh, southern Punjab and western Rajasthan

ledger.note: c. 270: Sindh, southern Punjab and western Rajasthan appear in the Satrap shape. Page-silent as to date and as to owner: the Rudradaman page lists Sindhu-Sauvira, Maru and Kukura among Rudradaman's lands in 150, and Cliopatria draws the same land as Eastern Kushan up to 269. The Western Satraps page names Rudrasena II (256-278) and Visvasena (293-304) as rulers of this time.

c. 306: part of Rajasthan passes to the Yaudheyas. Page-silent on the year; the Rudradaman page says Rudradaman subdued the Yaudheyas in Haryana and that they 'later regained independence'. 306 is where Cliopatria's Yaudheya row begins.

region.text: Rajasthan, half of Sindh and southern Punjab

ledger.note: c. 347: Samudragupta's Guptas take Rajasthan, half of Sindh and the southern Punjab. The page dates his conquests to no year: reign c. 335-375, direct control 'from the Ravi east to the Brahmaputra, with a southwest line from Karnal to Bhilsa'; the Shaka-Murundas of the Allahabad pillar are read as the Western Kshatrapas of Ujjain (Jayaswal, V. A. Smith) and at Eran his inscription 'may have replaced' Sridharavarman's. 347 is Cliopatria's year.

region.text: Malwa, Gujarat and the Arabian Sea coast: 'conquered Malwa after defeating the Western Kshatrapas'; reached 'the Arabian Sea coast in present-day Gujarat'

ledger.note: 397-409: Chandragupta II fights the last Kshatrapa, Rudrasimha III, for Malwa and Gujarat. The page dates the victory tentatively to between 397 and 409 and the last Kshatrapa coin to Shaka year 310 or 319 (388 or 397); the first campaign is not dated, so the window's start is used.
409: the war ends in Gupta victory; Chandragupta II's coins dated 409 resemble Kshatrapa coins, the Garuda replacing the Kshatrapa symbol; his Sanchi inscription of 412-413 records his victories.

region.text: the last Satrap realm: Malwa, Gujarat, Saurashtra, Sindh coast and western Rajasthan

ledger.note: 409: Chandragupta II ends the Western Satraps. 'The campaigns of Chandragupta II brought an end to nearly four centuries of Saka rule on the subcontinent' (Western Satraps page); the Natya-darpana has him killing Rudrasimha III, undated. The infobox says 415 and gives Rudrasimha III 388-415; this dossier follows the Chandragupta II page's upper bound of 409 and Cliopatria's last shape.

wars.name: Kshatrapa-Satavahana wars of Nasik Cave 10
wars.outcome: The Nasik Cave 10 inscriptions record Kshatrapa victories over the Satavahanas in 105-106.
wars.note: The page does not reconcile this with the later victory of Gautamiputra Satakarni over Nahapana; no border moved in Cliopatria.

wars.name: Gautamiputra Satakarni's war on Nahapana

zones.text: Nahapana's land in northern Konkan, Nasik and Poona; Gautamiputra 'rooted out the Khakharata family'

wars.outcome: Gautamiputra defeated Nahapana and restruck his coins (Jogalthembi hoard, Nashik district); the Kshaharata line ends.
wars.note: Dated c. 124 (Dhavalikar, the 18th regnal year), after 71 (Fynes) or 78 (Bhandare); the 'from' year is the earliest of the three. The Gautamiputra page's reign dates run from 60-85 to 106-130.

wars.name: Rudradaman I's wars with the Satavahanas

zones.text: the former Nahapana lands, 'except Poona and Nasik'

wars.outcome: Rudradaman defeated Satakarni twice but spared him because of their family ties; his daughter married Vashishtiputra Satakarni and Aparanta went to Satakarni as dowry.
wars.note: Which Satavahana king was defeated is disputed: Gautamiputra (Bhandarkar, Sircar), Vashishtiputra (Rapson) or Shivaskanda (Sen, Higham), per the Gautamiputra and Satavahana pages.

wars.name: Rudradaman I's campaign against the Yaudheyas
wars.outcome: Rudradaman 'by force destroyed the Yaudheyas who were loath to submit' (Junagadh inscription); they later regained independence.
wars.note: Years are the reign; the inscription is dated 150. No Cliopatria shape puts Haryana in the Satrap realm, so no border event is recorded.

wars.name: Yajna Sri Satakarni's reconquest of the Satrap south
wars.outcome: Yajna Sri Satakarni defeated the Western Satraps and reconquered their southern regions.
wars.note: Reign 170-199 (Sen) or ending 181 (Higham); Cliopatria's change is in 184.

wars.name: Samudragupta's campaigns in the west

zones.text: Eran, where his inscription may have replaced Sridharavarman's

wars.outcome: Samudragupta reduced the forest kings, made the Yaudheyas and Malavas tributaries and may have ousted the Shaka Sridharavarman at Eran; the page dates none of it to a year.
wars.note: Years are the reign (c. 335-375). Direct Gupta control reached a southwest line from Karnal to Bhilsa (Majumdar's view).

wars.name: Gupta-Saka War (Chandragupta II)
wars.outcome: Chandragupta II defeated the Western Kshatrapas (Rudrasimha III) and annexed Malwa and Gujarat; the Satrap state ends.
wars.note: Victory dated tentatively to between 397 and 409; Ramagupta's failed campaign is told in the Natya-darpana, undated.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the realm is known from inscriptions (Junagadh 150, Nasik caves, Sanchi), coin hoards and Ptolemy's list, not from lines. The 130-150 realm of Rudradaman is the best attested (the Junagadh list of lands).

notes:
Pages opened: nine, the whole of the 9-page budget (Western Satraps, Nahapana, Rudradaman, Chashtana, Gautamiputra Satakarni, Chandragupta II, Samudragupta, Satavahana dynasty, Vakataka dynasty). The Kushan Empire pages are cited only inside the kushan-empire dossier.

Every counterpart was checked against the Cliopatria geometry: the 43 shape is 1,330 of 1,331 cells cut from the Indo-Scythian shape; the 127 growth is 1,201 cells of the Satavahana shapes of -27 to 126; the 154, 184 and 224 changes match the Satavahana shapes; 260 is 453 of 453 cells into the Vakataka shape; 270 is 1,339 of 1,339 cells from the Eastern Kushans; 306 is 230 of 235 cells into the Yaudheya shape; 347 is 1,109 of 1,112 cells into the Gupta shape. Only the owners and the page-given reasons are mine; every year after 127 except 397-409 is Cliopatria's and flagged confidence 1.

Corrections: (1) the state begins c. 35, not 43; (2) it ends 409, not 489: Cliopatria's two 55 km2 shapes of 476-489 are stubs next to the Maitraka row and are marked wrong; there is no shape for 410-475 (the two stubs are under one H3 cell, so the --resolve warnings on their corrections are expected); (3) Nasik and Poona are cut out of the 127 shape; (4) the infobox says the state ended in 415, the Chandragupta II page tentatively between 397 and 409 (coins dated 409 carry the Garuda); 409 is used.

Not settled:
- Nahapana's chronology (24-70, 66-71, 119-124, or ending 78) leaves the Kshaharata shape of 43-126 unchecked; the Satraps page puts Konkan, Nasik and Poona in his realm, Cliopatria puts them with the Satavahanas.
- The Junagadh inscription (150) lists Sindhu-Sauvira (Sindh and Multan), Maru and Kukura as Rudradaman's; Cliopatria draws Sindh and part of Rajasthan as Kushan until 270 and then Satrap. A page that adjudicates (the Junagadh inscription itself, or the Kushan side) is missing; the Kushan dossier and this one record the Satraps as Kushan vassals for 127-150 (confidence 1) because the Rudradaman page calls the Kushans his suzerains and the Western Satraps page reports that Chastana may have been a Kushan feudatory (the Mathura statue) and that the Rabatak inscription claims Ujjain for Kanishka.
- Nasik is in the Satrap shape from 224, while the Satavahana page names the Abhira dynasty as the western successor 'around Nashik' and the Abhira dynasty page has them rule Nasik from 203 with the Satraps' consent; the 224 Nasik gain now names abhira-dynasty.
- Sanchi-Vidisha was re-established under Rudrasena II (255-278) per the Satraps page, but is in the shape from 224 and through 409; at Eran the Samudragupta page suggests the Guptas replaced Sridharavarman (339-368) in the mid-4th century, yet the shape keeps Eran to 409.
- The Rudradaman and Satavahana pages disagree on who was defeated and on whether Aparanta was dowry; the Satavahana dossier (another group) dates the same events to 124, 127 and 154.
- No ruler strip: the page's list is partial and overlapping (Jivadaman 178-181 and 197-198, Rudrasimha I 178-197, Rudrasena II 256-278, Visvasena 293-304, Rudrasimha II 304-348, Yasodaman II 317-332, Rudradaman II 332-348, Sridharavarman 339-368, Rudrasimha III 388-415).
- Minnagara, a capital in the infobox, is not located on any page opened; Bharuch is a placeholder for 35-126.

Counterparts without a dossier of their own: none; slugs used are indo-scythians, satavahana-dynasty, vakataka-kingdom, eastern-kushans, yaudheya-republic, gupta-empire, maitraka-dynasty. The Kshaharata (Nahapana) and Kardamaka lines are one state here (rename 78), as in the page's infobox. The Abhira dynasty of Nashik has no dossier and would be a counterpart for 224-260.

Repair (sa-02-c-fixed, 2026-10-19), answering the reviewer:
- Vassal pair added (127-150, counterpart kushan-empire, Western Satraps page, confidence 1), agreed with kushan-empire, which moved from 127-225. The page says 'vassals of the Kushans, at least in the early period until Rudradaman I conquered the Yaudheyas'; the reviewer's c. 130 end was considered and not taken (the conquest is undated within Rudradaman's reign 130-150, and the Junagadh inscription is dated 150). The Chastana page (read 2026-10-19) gives no date for any Kushan relation.
- 35-42 overlap with indo-scythians: kept at 35 (page: 'Established: 35'). indo-scythians /ledger/13 and its keyframe 43 put the same land in the Indo-Scythian shape until 42; sa-02-b should move its loss to 35. Not settled between the dossiers; reported.
- Ujjain capital: Bharuch to 126, Ujjain from 127, the first shape that contains it.
- 127 gain: dated 127 (Cliopatria; Rudradaman's reign starts 130) to agree with the 127 keyframe and satavahana-dynasty /ledger/5; confidence 1.
